messages.content: You are a skeptical senior world-model security researcher.

{"prompt": "Propose one materially different, high-novelty world-model security mechanism under a strict legal-action truthful-observation threat model. Exclude negative transfer, OOD, forgetting, rollout compounding, uncertainty, support/positivity holes, action Jacobians, stale state, prompt leakage, temporal copulas, and generic representation drift. Available carriers: TD-MPC2, MBRL-Lib, WorldAgen, DreamerV3 RSSM code, ScienceWorld/DiscoveryWorld. Need a causal invariant, native short gate, repair, and two-task scale path. Return JSON keys claim,operation,invariant,mediator,carrier,gate,baselines,novelty_risk,decision. Be skeptical and use conditional_go only if executable."}

message.content:
{
  "claim": "A causal-contrast integrity gate can detect a corrupted or misleading short-horizon world-model transition even when every executed action is legal and every returned observation is truthful. The claim is limited: it detects disagreement on explicitly declared observable predicate effects, not arbitrary model error or long-horizon compromise.",
  "operation": "At a checkpoint s_t, select two legal actions a and b that differ on one declared intervention target, execute each once in the real environment from cloned state where cloning is supported, and record truthful observations o_{t+1}^a and o_{t+1}^b. Run the same pair through the model. Convert both outcomes into a fixed verifier vector of observable predicate changes, v(o_t,o_{t+1}). Compare the model and environment action contrasts: Delta_env = v(o_t,o_{t+1}^a) - v(o_t,o_{t+1}^b), Delta_model = v_hat(s_t,a) - v_hat(s_t,b). Accept only when the signed contrast, affected-predicate support, and bounded magnitude agree. The intervention pair is sampled from a precomputed legal-action table, not generated by the model.",
  "invariant": "For every declared intervention pair (a,b) and verifier predicate subset P, the causal contrast of the next observation is invariant to the model implementation: I[sign(Delta_env[P]) = sign(Delta_model[P]) and support(Delta_env[P]) = support(Delta_model[P])] = 1, subject to an explicitly measured tolerance for magnitude. This is a local structural invariant over legal action contrasts, not a representation, uncertainty, OOD, or Jacobian invariant.",
  "mediator": "A fixed, non-trainable observable-effect mediator v maps an observation pair to changes in typed predicates such as object-location, containment, switch-state, inventory, temperature-bin, or textually stated world facts. In ScienceWorld this can be derived from the symbolic observation/state interface. In DiscoveryWorld it can use the environment's fact/property interface. For pixel-only TD-MPC2 settings, the mechanism is not considered executable until an audited deterministic predicate extractor is supplied; a learned latent embedding is not an acceptable mediator.",
  "carrier": "Primary carrier: TD-MPC2 with an auxiliary one-step effect head and a verifier-side contrast buffer. Secondary carrier: DreamerV3 RSSM by applying the gate to the RSSM one-step transition decoder. MBRL-Lib is suitable for the paired-action data collection and constrained repair loop. WorldAgen is deferred unless it exposes deterministic legal-action replay and typed observable predicates.",
  "gate": "Native short gate: one checkpoint, one legal action pair, two one-step environment calls, and two model evaluations. Reject if any protected predicate has a sign or support mismatch, or if normalized magnitude error exceeds a prespecified threshold calibrated on clean training rollouts. The gate must run before accepting a model-generated transition for planning. It does not require an uncertainty estimate, rollout, action Jacobian, stale state, or distribution-shift detector.",
  "repair": "On rejection, do not globally retrain or alter the encoder. Freeze the representation and reward components, fit only the one-step transition/effect head using the two truthful observations and a small replay set of previously verified contrasts, with a constrained objective enforcing the observed predicate contrast. Re-run the same pair. If two repairs fail, disable model-based branching for the affected predicate subset and use real one-step environment interaction; report the model as unverified rather than silently repairing it.",
  "baselines": [
    "Un-gated TD-MPC2 or DreamerV3 RSSM planning.",
    "One-step observation reconstruction and reward-prediction checks without action-pair contrasts.",
    "Ensemble disagreement or stochastic latent variance gates, excluded from the proposed mechanism but useful as negative controls.",
    "Random legal-action pair checks without a declared intervention target.",
    "Ablation using an unconstrained learned latent mediator instead of fixed typed predicates."
  ],
  "novelty_risk": "Moderate-to-high. The paired-action test resembles finite-difference system identification, causal probing, and model-based consistency checks, so novelty depends on the security framing and the repair protocol rather than on the existence of action pairs alone. The strongest differentiator is the signed typed-predicate causal checksum plus selective transition-head repair under a legal-action/truthful-observation threat model. It will not detect corruption outside the declared predicate set, corruption that preserves all tested contrasts, or an environment whose two actions have genuinely nondeterministic effects. Cloned-state support and deterministic predicate extraction are practical blockers.",
  "decision": "conditional_go: implement first on two ScienceWorld tasks sharing an explicit predicate schema. Require a reproducible legal-action-pair table, deterministic verifier vectors, clean-trajectory threshold calibration, injected transition-head corruption tests, and an ablation against reconstruction-only gates. Do not claim deployment readiness or cross-task scaling until the gate detects corruption on held-out intervention pairs without exceeding an agreed false-reject budget."
}
